input: Research Tesla (tesla.com) for a hedge fund

catalysts.claim: Confirmed annual meeting on December 3, 2026: shareholders will vote on directors, executive compensation and auditor ratification; announced as of 2026-10-19.
Management targets 400 MW of AI training compute by year-end 2026; target as_of 2026-10-21.
As of 2026-09-30, sales restrictions on Tesla's SpaceX investment expire in December 2026: a Tesla-held asset unlock, not a Tesla-share lock-up.
As of 2026-11-10, Wall Street Horizon forecasts quarterly earnings after market close on January 27, 2027; explicitly UNCONFIRMED by Tesla.
As of 2026-11-10, Wall Street Horizon infers quarterly earnings after market close on April 21, 2027; not company-confirmed.

results_vs_guidance.claim: Latest reported quarter, Q3 2026: revenue missed company-compiled consensus at $28.05 billion versus $28.34 billion; adjusted EPS beat at $0.48 versus $0.45; GAAP EPS missed at $0.22 versus $0.23. Comparison updated as_of 2026-10-28.
Quarter ended 2026-09-30: operating cash flow was $6.263 billion, capex $4.732 billion and free cash flow $1.531 billion.

Pre-report consensus as_of 2026-10-19 expected quarterly operating cash flow of $3.267 billion, capex of $7.771 billion and negative free cash flow of $4.506 billion; these were analyst estimates, not guidance.
Quarter ended 2026-09-30: automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits reached 18.1%, versus 16.3% in the preceding quarter.
Prior management guidance as_of 2026-07-22 called for annual capex in excess of $25 billion.
Current guidance as_of 2026-10-21 calls for annual capex in excess of $20 billion.

As of 2026-10-21, the published volume outlook emphasizes maximum factory utilization and demand, supply-chain readiness and fleet allocation; it provides no numerical revenue, EPS or delivery target.

event_driven.claim: As of 2026-10-21, disinterested directors are reviewing closer SpaceX ties, including a business combination; completion requires committee recommendation and any necessary shareholder approval.
As of 2026-09-30, Tesla disclosed an AI-hardware asset acquisition for $1.95 billion in stock/equity awards, including $1.73 billion subject to service or performance conditions.

credit_signals.claim: As of 2026-09-30, cash and short-term investments were $45.447 billion; unsecured facilities had $30 billion undrawn. Tesla reported material compliance with financial debt covenants.
As of 2026-09-30, debt principal was $9.28 billion, including $1.32 billion current.
As of 2026-09-30, China working-capital principal was $5.966 billion, maturing October 2026–September 2027; long-term classification reflects Tesla's stated intent and ability to refinance.

Facilities signed as_of 2026-09-29: $20 billion delayed-draw term loan matures September 29, 2029; $8 billion revolver September 29, 2031; $2 billion revolver September 28, 2027. Tesla did not plan drawings during 2026.

Credit agreement as_of 2026-09-29 requires at least $5 billion consolidated liquidity. Certain merger/change-of-control provisions depend on investment-grade ratings from at least two agencies; transaction structure and ratings therefore matter.

alternative_signals.claim: Hiring snapshot as_of 2026-11-10: Tesla advertises an Optimus Hardware Robotics Technical Program Manager internship in Palo Alto for winter/spring 2027; an opening, not evidence of net headcount growth.

Trade reporting as_of 2026-11-09 says Cybercab general-assembly manager Jody Kerns left for Rivian in October; Musk also acknowledged limited engineering resources when explaining Cybertruck reprioritization.
October 2026 registrations rose 248% in Sweden, 131% in Norway and 34% in Denmark year over year; Reuters cautions that easier comparisons and incentives contributed.
US pricing snapshot as_of 2026-11-10: Tesla lists supervised FSD at $99 monthly. This verifies the current price, not a recent price change.
As of 2026-09-30, active FSD subscriptions reached 1.74 million, up 67% year over year; Tesla's definition includes upfront purchases and monthly subscriptions, excluding free trials.
Trade reporting as_of 2026-10-23 quotes management describing Megapack as nearly sold out for 2027; this is management commentary, not a quantified contracted-revenue backlog.

insider_and_ownership.claim: On 2026-09-08, CFO Vaibhav Taneja sold 2,605.75 shares at $360.134, leaving 25,972.25 directly held. Form 4 says the sale automatically satisfied RSU tax withholding, rather than discretionary selling.
BlackRock's amended 13G reports 196,348,742 beneficially owned shares, or 4.96%, as_of 2026-09-30; it checks ownership at or below 5%. No selling inference is made without a comparable prior filing.
Proxy disclosure as_of 2026-10-19: Musk exercised 303,960,630 options on June 16, 2026; 17,531,857 shares were withheld for net settlement. This was compensation exercise, not open-market buying.

risks.claim: Regulatory execution risk: NHTSA opened a Cybercab self-certification audit on 2026-09-04 following deployment. Compliance scrutiny could constrain rollout; no resolution date was verified as_of 2026-11-10.
Supply risk: Tesla identifies battery availability as limiting vehicle production despite strong backlog, as_of 2026-10-21; demand need not translate promptly into deliveries.

Cash-quality risk: for the quarter ended 2026-09-30, working-capital changes contributed $2.59 billion against $1.53 billion free cash flow; trade analysis highlights unpaid purchases and accrued liabilities.
Competitive risk: despite October 2026 registration growth, Tesla's Danish market share was 0.73%, below several Chinese competitors; regional recovery is not uniform.

Transaction-incentive risk: proxy terms as_of 2026-10-19 accelerate vesting of Musk's restricted shares from his exercised option award upon qualifying change of control; shareholder and executive incentives warrant scrutiny.
As of 2026-09-30, Autopilot litigation included $200 million punitive damages plus Tesla's 33% share of $129 million compensatory damages; post-trial relief was denied and appeal remained pending.

output.research_view: As of 2026-11-10, the central question is whether improving automotive margins and software adoption can fund the autonomy and robotics build-out without relying on working-capital timing. Treat the SpaceX review as unpriced transaction optionality, not an agreed deal; prioritize cash conversion, Cybercab regulatory progress and capital-spending execution over launch headlines.

cost_basis: tokens x list price + $10 per 1K web search calls
